candidates_ranked_by_confidence.notes: Unifies 'Raised to X From Y by Firm', 'Cut to X From Y by Firm', 'Initiated at X by Firm', and the rarer 'Stock Upgraded/Downgraded to X' phrasing under one rating-tier vocabulary (confirmed via a full scan of every distinct rating word appearing in this template across the cached corpus -- 21 distinct tier words, all accounted for above). Highest-value fix found: FinBERT gets Initiated-at-Buy right only ~21% of the time (23/108 Bull, rest Neutral), and for Cut-to-Underweight/Underperform it is actually BACKWARDS 9/23 times (scored Bullish on a downgrade). The rating tier itself is the ground truth here, not the Raised/Cut/Initiated verb -- reading it directly removes the ambiguity FinBERT is failing on. A naive 50/50 average with FinBERT's own read was considered and rejected -- confirmed on this exact candidate that it disagrees with the regex's ground-truth tier read on 91/471 (19%) of matched articles, the same kind of dilution the project's earlier headline+body A/B test already found and rejected -- so this stays a full override, same as every other fast_path_score rule.
